summary: Ralph Lilley Turner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1906–1910). He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Banaras Hindu University, and served as Director of SOAS University of London (1922–1957).

Indologist Ralph T. H. Griffith was educated at The Queen's College, Oxford, studying under Horace Hayman Wilson. He became Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford in 1849, served in the Indian Educational Service, and was Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1861–1878).
Working in philosophy, Ralph Waldo Emerson was educated at Harvard College and Harvard University (~1817–1821) and later studied at Harvard Divinity School (~1825–1826).

Ram Chandra Kak worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Sri Pratap College and trained under John Marshall (1914–1919), he served as superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India and Director of Jammu and Kashmir's Department of Archæology and Research (1919–1929).

Indologist and linguist Ram Karan Sharma earned his MA at Patna University and his PhD under Murray B. Emeneau at UC Berkeley. He served as vice chancellor of Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1974–1980) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1984–1985).

Ram Mohan Roy was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He founded the Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), Mir'at al-Akhbar (1822), Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Vedanta College (1826), and Brahmo Samaj (1828).

Working in Indology, history, and archaeology, Ram Niwas Pandey studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and the Institute of Archaeology, Archaeological Survey of India, completing doctoral research under Hit Narayan Jha.

Ram Shankar Tripathi worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as Head of the Department of Bauddhadarśana at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1989–1998) and Dean of the Faculty of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Historian and Indologist Ram Sharan Sharma earned degrees from Patna University and SOAS (PhD under Arthur Llewellyn Basham). He headed history at Patna University (1958–1973), was professor and dean at the University of Delhi, and founded the ICHR.
Rama Misra Shastri was an Indologist and philosopher who served as assistant Professor of Sáṅkhya at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1882 and 1914.

Rama Nath Sharma studied under Raghunatha Sharma and Ramaprasada Tripathi, earning degrees from BHU, Allahabad, Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar, and Rochester (PhD). He taught at Allahabad and held professorships at the University of Rochester (1971–1976) and University of Hawaiʻi (~1976).

Indologist and linguist Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar studied at Elphinstone College, University of Mumbai, and University of Göttingen under Martin Haug. He held professorships at Elphinstone College and Deccan College, later serving as Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1893–1894).

Ramaprasad Chanda worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after graduating from Scottish Church College. He worked with the Archaeological Survey of India and served as Superintendent of the Archaeological Section at the Indian Museum (1921–1932).

Indologist Ramaranjan Mukherji earned his BA and PhD at the University of Calcutta and a DLitt at Jadavpur University. He headed Sanskrit at Jadavpur (1956) and served as vice chancellor of Burdwan University (1970–1984) and Rabindra Bharati University (~1984–1987).
Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Vidyapith and at L.D. Arts College (attested 1938).

Indologist Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar was educated at the University of Mumbai and Heidelberg University. He served as Honorary Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1939–2001) and was Professor of Sanskrit and Dean of Arts at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Ramendra Sundar Tribedi worked in Indology and philosophy. After studying at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta (~1882–1887), he held posts at Presidency University and served as Principal of Surendranath College beginning in 1892.

Historian and Indologist Ramesh Chandra Majumdar studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta (PhD 1918). He served as professor, dean, and Provost at the University of Dhaka (1921–1942), and as Principal at BHU (1950–1952) and Nagpur University (1955).

Ramesh Shankar Gupte worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 1967, he headed History & Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and was a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest, Salem, and Winston-Salem State.
Ramin Etesami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at International Buddhist College under the supervision of Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina (attested 2015).
